fora.v1.AcceptableRestriction.description:
AcceptableRestriction — the limits a query operates within on one restriction
 axis, expressed in the same RestrictionKind vocabulary that terms use. The
 Exchange/Broker MAY pre-select offers whose term restrictions fall within
 these as a convenience (see Restriction); it is NOT enforcement — the agent
 self-selects and bears compliance.

axis.description:
Which axis (same enum as Restriction.kind): FUNCTION / GEOGRAPHY /
 USER_TYPE / OTHER.
axis.title: Restriction Kind

values.description:
The values the query operates within on this axis — same token vocabulary
 as the terms (e.g. FUNCTION ["ai-train"], GEOGRAPHY ["US", "EU"]).

fora.v1.AcceptableRestriction.title: Acceptable Restriction

amount.description: Exact decimal string (not a float), e.g. "19.99". Denominated in `currency`.

fora.v1.Delegation.description:
The token is a signed JWT (token_format "jwt"; the field stays open for a
 future format) carrying a holder-bound delegation chain. Its claims are the
 AUTHORITATIVE source of the grant; the plaintext fields below (scopes,
 expires_at, max_spend_cents, …) are a mirror the Exchange MAY use for fast
 pre-filtering before it verifies the token. A mirror establishes nothing: it
 cannot grant a scope, extend validity or raise a cap beyond what the signed
 chain says.

 The profile — chain encoding and limits, protected header, claims, clock
 leeway, issuer, audience and holder-binding rules, the verification
 procedure and the outcome of each failure — is the "Delegation" section of
 the authentication page and is not restated here; the Go SDK verifier
 (sdk/go/helpers) and the shared chain cases are derived from it. What a
 field reader must know: the grant is bound to a holder key by `cnf.jkt`, and
 the key a request proves possession of MUST hash to the terminal token's
 `cnf.jkt` (the RFC 9421 request signer on a direct call; on a purchase a
 Broker relayed, the key each item's AgentAcceptance verifies under), so a
 token possessed without its private key grants nothing. On a query a Broker
 originated nothing can pass that binding: the Exchange does not honour the
 delegation, answers as if none were present, and presents no term gated
 behind one (see LicenseTerm.scopes).

expires_at.description:
Mirror of the chain's earliest `exp`. The Exchange MUST reject an expired
 token; the signed `exp` values decide, not this field.

ext_critical.description:
Critical extension keys (COSE crit pattern, RFC 9052).
 Lists keys within ext that the consumer MUST understand.
 Unknown keys in this list → reject with UNKNOWN_CRITICAL_EXTENSION.
 Empty (default) → all ext keys are safe to ignore.

issuer.description:
Mirror of the ROOT token's `iss`, the identity configured with the trusted
 key (never an intermediate or terminal issuer). Informational: the
 Exchange never discovers a key from it, through OIDC, JWKS or otherwise.

max_accesses.description:
Maximum number of accesses allowed under this delegation.
 Exchange tracks cumulative access count against this cap.
 Deny with DENIAL_REASON_QUOTA_EXCEEDED when count >= limit.
 For subscriptions with "10,000 accesses/month", this carries the ceiling.

max_spend_cents.description:
Maximum spend in currency minor units (e.g., cents for USD).
 Exchange tracks cumulative spend against this cap.

principal_domain.description:
Mirror of the ROOT token's `iss`, the configured trust anchor's identity.
 Informational: no key is looked up from it, and it establishes no trust.

principal_id.description:
Principal's identifier (e.g., "user@acme.com", "marketdata.example.com").
 Informational; not read by the verifier.

quota_period.description:
Quota reset period. How often the access/spend counters reset.
 Example: 30 days for monthly subscriptions — "2592000s" on the wire
 (proto-JSON encodes Duration as seconds; "720h" is not accepted).
 When absent, the quota is lifetime (bounded only by expires_at).

revocation_uri.description:
Informational. Revocation lookup is not part of the delegation profile:
 the verifier never fetches this URI. A chain is invalidated early by
 withdrawing the configured root key.

scopes.description:
Mirror of the terminal token's effective scopes. In the chain, each
 child's scopes are covered by its parent's under the scope-matching rule
 on Requester.scopes (attenuation — can only narrow, not widen).

token.description:
Token bytes. A JWT (base64url-encoded JWS). At most 32768 bytes: the
 complete chain, every embedded parent included, must fit. The limit is a
 wire rule, checked before the token is parsed and independent of whether
 the bytes are a valid JWT; a longer token is an invalid request, not a
 per-item denial.

token_format.description:
Token format: "jwt" (default). Empty is treated as "jwt". The field stays
 open for a future format.

fora.v1.Delegation.title: Delegation — Scoped, time-limited, spend-capped credential.

budget_period.description:
Budget period (e.g. "2592000s" = 30 days; proto-JSON encodes Duration
 as seconds).

budget_scope.description:
Budget scope identifier: whose budget this is.
 E.g. "user:u-12345" for per-user budgets, "team:eng" for per-team.

delivery_preference.description: Preferred delivery methods, in order of preference.

exchanges.description:
Authorized Exchange domains, in the shape "Request recipient" defines in the
 file header. Broker queries only these. This is a FILTER over third parties,
 not an address — the recipient of the request carrying it is a separate
 question.

max_data_age.description:
Only relevant for DYNAMIC resources. Ignored for STATIC (content is
 immutable) and LIVE (content doesn't exist yet).

 Examples:
   7 days   — "credit report updated within the last week"
   1 hour   — "stock snapshot from the last hour"
   30 days  — "drug interaction database updated this month"
max_data_age.title:
Maximum acceptable age of resource data. The Broker SHOULD
 exclude offers where (now - Offer.data_as_of) exceeds this duration.

max_hops.description:
Maximum number of hops the agent will allow its discovery to travel. It
 rides only on DiscoveryRequest, which terminates at the Broker, and a
 Broker originates its own queries rather than forwarding the agent's
 request, so no party receives or enforces it in this version: an Exchange
 never sees it, and an Exchange's own cap is
 WellKnownManifest.max_intermediary_hops. The field is kept for multi-hop
 Broker discovery, an open protocol question. Absent = no cap stated.

max_price.description: Maximum price the agent is willing to pay.

max_unit_cost.description: Maximum effective cost per unit, as an exact decimal string (not a float).

period_budget.description: Per-period budget limit for the budget_scope.

preferred_exchanges.description:
Exchanges the agent has existing relationships with (subscriptions,
 contracts). The Broker SHOULD prefer these when resource is
 available — subscription resource has zero marginal cost.

reporting_capable.description: Whether the agent supports post-usage reporting.

fora.v1.Requester.description:
Carries identity and entitlements ONLY — who is asking and what they are
 entitled to (scopes, delegation). What they are asking for (uris) and the
 limits they will operate within (acceptable_restrictions) belong to the ask,
 not the identity, and live on ResourceQuery / DiscoveryRequest. The Exchange
 verifies identity via the RFC 9421 request signature, then presents the
 terms the requester's stated scopes cover (see LicenseTerm.scopes). Billing
 needs nothing from this message:
 the Exchange resolves the agent's account (RegisterResponse.billing_ref) from
 what authenticates the agent, never from a value the caller merely states
 (see "Accounts" in the file header).

delegation.description:
Optional delegation — present when the requester acts on behalf of
 another entity (user, organization, upstream agent). On a query a Broker
 originated it is not honoured, because the Broker signs alone and nothing
 on that leg can pass its holder binding; the Exchange answers as if none
 were present (see Delegation).

domain.description:
- Direct request. The agent's own RFC 9421 signature arrives because
     the agent sent the request itself. The verifier resolves the agent's
     keys from the COVERED `Signature-Agent` member, never from this field.
     It then MUST require this field to name that same directory: the host
     of the origin that member names, compared by
     the identity rule "Request recipient" defines (the shape check first,
     then case-folded, an absent port the same as ":443", a subdomain a
     different party). A mismatch is refused as UNAUTHENTICATED with
     `request_auth_failure` SIGNATURE_INVALID: the signature verifies, but
     not for the requester the body names. A Broker applies this rule at
     BrokerService.ExecuteTransaction. At BrokerService.Resolve it refuses
     nothing for this field: every query it originates names the host of
     the origin that member names (see DiscoveryRequest.requester). An
     Exchange applies it on every request whose signer it does not admit as
     a Broker; a mismatch from a signer it does admit is a relayed request,
     one of the two cases below.
   - Purchase relayed through a Broker. BrokerService.ExecuteTransaction
     re-packages the purchase, so the request signature and the covered
     `Signature-Agent` member are the Broker's. They say only that the call comes
     from the Broker, and they sign no purchase. The Exchange MUST verify
     each item's AgentAcceptance, and the AgentRequestAcceptance, against
     the Ed25519 keys currently valid in the directory this field names
     (see AgentRequestAcceptance), never against the Broker's key. Those
     acceptances are the only agent signatures the Exchange sees, and the
     purchase belongs to the account of the directory they verify under
     (see "Accounts" in the file header).
   - Broker-led discovery. A ResourceQuery a Broker originated carries no agent
     signature, so nothing on that leg authenticates this field: it is the
     Broker's statement, under the Broker's own signature, of whom it
     queries for. A delegation on such a query is not honoured (see
     Delegation).
domain.title:
REQUIRED. Bare host of the requester's key directory: the WBA directory at
 {domain}/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory that publishes the
 agent's Ed25519 keys. It carries the bare-host shape "Request recipient"
 defines in the file header (a port allowed), for the same structural
 reason: a scheme, path or query smuggled in here would choose what gets
 fetched, not merely from where. It is never a free label. Every verifier
 reads it as the name of that directory, and the rule that binds it depends
 on whether the request is direct or relayed, which the receiver decides as
 "Direct and relayed requests" in the file header states:

ext_critical.description:
Critical extension keys (COSE crit pattern, RFC 9052).
 Lists keys within ext that the consumer MUST understand.
 Unknown keys in this list → reject with UNKNOWN_CRITICAL_EXTENSION.
 Empty (default) → all ext keys are safe to ignore.

id.description:
REQUIRED. A free label the agent chooses for attribution (e.g.
 "agent-research-bot-001"), 1 to 255 characters. Use it to tell apart the
 sub-agents or end customers that share one key directory. It is never
 identity: no verifier finds keys from it, and no party trusts it for an
 authentication or authorization decision. The requester's identity is
 `domain` together with the key that verifies. The acceptance signatures
 cover this label (see AgentAcceptancePayload), so a relaying Broker cannot
 rewrite it, but its value is still only what the agent says.

scopes.description:
EXISTENCE HIDING. A requester never learns about a resource outside its
 scopes. When the scopes leave no presentable offer for a resource, the
 Exchange answers with no offers and no absence reason (an OfferGroup with
 empty `offers` and `absence_reason` unset), exactly as for any resource
 with nothing to offer. A Broker relaying that answer adds no reason of its
 own. At purchase, an offer the Exchange presented is honoured until it
 expires, so a scope refusal cannot arise there. No reason in the protocol
 reports a scope shortfall: OFFER_ABSENCE_REASON_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT and
 DENIAL_REASON_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT are deprecated and never sent.

 Scope format: colon-separated segments, "{domain}:{permission}" or
 "{profile}:{permission}", optionally multi-segment ("dist:US:CA");
 matching is segment-wise per the rule below (no implicit hierarchy).
 Examples:
   "credit:read"                — can access credit reports
   "subscription:marketdata-2026" — has active MarketData subscription
   "academic:*"                 — full access to academic resources
   "internal:reports"           — can access internal reports
   "*"                         — unrestricted (public Exchange default)

 Matching is SEGMENT-WISE (":" separated). A granted scope G covers a
 required scope R iff, segment by segment, each G segment equals the
 corresponding R segment or is "*"; a terminal "*" matches all remaining
 segments, of which there must be at least one. There is NO implicit prefix
 match, and a grant NARROWER than the requirement does not cover it (G must
 be equal-to-or-broader than R), so a grant with more segments than the
 requirement never covers it, even when its last segment is "*". A "*" in R
 is a literal segment: a narrow grant never covers a wildcard requirement.
 Matching is case-sensitive and never trims. Examples: "dist:*" covers
 "dist:US", "dist:US:CA" and "dist:US:*" but not "dist"; "dist:US:*" covers
 "dist:US:CA" but not "dist:EU" or "dist:US"; "publisher:*:read" covers
 "publisher:news:read" but not "publisher:news:*"; bare "dist" covers only
 "dist"; granted "dist:US:CA" does NOT cover required "dist:US"; "*" covers
 everything. This same rule governs LicenseTerm.scopes and the attenuation
 of a delegation child against its parent — one algorithm protocol-wide.

 When empty, Exchange applies its default access policy (typically
 returns all publicly available resources).
scopes.title:
Entitlement scopes: the requester's own statement of what it is entitled
 to. On a query a Broker originated, they are the Broker's statement for the
 agent. They are signed and attributable, and the Exchange does not verify
 them. Scope coverage decides which terms the Exchange presents (see
 LicenseTerm.scopes, which also states when an Exchange MAY require a
 verified delegation); it is not access control. A false statement is
 traceable to the signing key, its directory and its account, and the
 agent's acceptance signs the scoped offer it buys; it is settled through
 reconciliation and the account relationship.

type.description: What kind of entity is making this request.
type.title: Requester Type

fora.v1.Requester.title: Requester — Universal identity for any FORA client.

acceptable_restrictions.description:
The limits the agent will operate within, per restriction axis — see
 AcceptableRestriction. The Broker forwards these to Exchanges in
 ResourceQuery.acceptable_restrictions. Advisory selection inputs, not
 enforcement.

constraints.description: Constraints for exchange filtering and offer selection.

ext_critical.description:
Critical extension keys (COSE crit pattern, RFC 9052).
 Lists keys within ext that the consumer MUST understand.
 Unknown keys in this list → reject with UNKNOWN_CRITICAL_EXTENSION.
 Empty (default) → all ext keys are safe to ignore.

query.description:
Search query for Broker-side resource discovery.
 Used when the agent doesn't know specific URIs but wants the Broker
 to find matching resources across Exchanges.
 When present, the Broker interprets the query and discovers resources
 across Exchanges on the agent's behalf. Results returned as Offers
 in DiscoveryResponse, same as for specific URI requests.
 Can be used alongside uris (specific URIs + search in one request).

requester.description:
Requester identity — who is making this request, the scopes it states.
 The Broker forwards this to Exchanges in ResourceQuery.requester, with
 Requester.domain the host of the origin that the covered `Signature-Agent`
 member of the agent's verified signature names. A Requester.domain that
 names another host is never forwarded, and the Broker answers the request
 all the same (see "Direct and relayed requests" in the file header).
 REQUIRED: a discovery names its requester, whose Requester.id and
 Requester.domain are required in turn.

search_filters.description:
Structured search filters (optional, alongside or instead of query).
 Keys are profile-specific: "academic.topic", "news.category",
 "legal.jurisdiction", etc. The Broker maps these to Exchange-specific
 query parameters.

supported_profiles.description:
The Broker MUST forward this list unchanged in
 ResourceQuery.supported_profiles on every query it sends an Exchange, and
 forward an absent list as absent. It does not route by it: which Exchanges
 it queries is decided on other grounds, and each Exchange answers for its
 own profiles (see ResourceQuery.supported_profiles).

 Examples: ["fora-academic-v1"] — agent working on literature review
supported_profiles.title: Domain extension profiles the agent understands.

uris.description:
Resource URIs the agent wants. The Broker forwards these to Exchanges in
 ResourceQuery.uris. Optional when `query` / `search_filters` drive
 Broker-side discovery instead.

ver.description:
FORA protocol version — "1.0". Stamped by the sender from a single
 constant; advisory on receive. See "Protocol version" in the file header.
